programme.title: Proof complexity: lower bounds toward NP ≠ coNP
programme.goal: Proved lower bounds (for all n; Lean-checked where the pipeline allows) on explicit tautology families in named propositional proof systems, or proved separations between systems, found with measurements that are exact at fixed n (resolution width, Nullstellensatz / polynomial-calculus / Sherali-Adams / SoS degree). Cook-Reckhow: NP ≠ coNP iff every proof system has superpolynomial lower bounds; this programme works where bounds are provable, the weak systems. Prior art, ground rules and the order of work are in direction.md.

targets.statement: The exact-measurement pipeline, reproduced on known ground. A `check.py`-style tool that, for a CNF family and n in a stated range, computes exactly: minimum resolution width (decision procedure for width-k refutations, Berkholz arXiv 1204.0775), Nullstellensatz degree and polynomial-calculus degree over F2 and F3 (linear algebra / degree-bounded Groebner), and Sherali-Adams degree (LP). Reproduce, with every computed n agreeing with the published bound: PHP^(n+1)_n (resolution width Omega(n); Nullstellensatz/PC degree), Tseitin on small expanders, random 3-CNF at density about 4.2, and the ordering principle GT_n as the negative control (width Omega(n) but polynomial resolution size, Bonet-Galesi 2001) - the pipeline must report GT_n's polynomial-size refutation and must not call it hard. Results are tables with status `measured`; solver refutations (CaDiCaL/kissat-style, python-sat) are upper bounds on size only.

A machine-checked resolution lower bound in Lean 4 (core, no sorry, `#print axioms` listing only propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound): formalise resolution refutations of CNFs and prove, for all n, either Haken's exponential lower bound for PHP^(n+1)_n or the Ben-Sasson-Wigderson width bound for PHP (width >= n/2-ish as stated in the source, with the size-width relation if feasible). State the definitions so that a refutation produced by a solver for small n could be checked against the same `Refutation` type (upper bound and lower bound for one family in one library). Before claiming: check AFP, Mathlib, Lean Zulip and arXiv for an existing formalisation (none was found on 2026-10-23).

Polynomial calculus across characteristics: an explicit, catalogue-named (or genuinely new) CNF family with a PROVED degree lower bound over F_p and a polynomial-size (or low-degree) refutation over F_q for p != q, where no such separation for that family is known; checked first against Nordström's Handbook of Satisfiability chapter (2021) and two years of ECCC. Target A's exact PC degree tables are the search tool; only growth with a stated combinatorial reason goes to a proof. Not before A.

Cutting planes: a new natural CNF family with a proved cutting-planes lower bound (interpolation or lifting), using Sherali-Adams / SoS degree and LP-relaxation rank as proxies. Tseitin is excluded (quasi-polynomial CP refutations, Dadush-Tiwari 2020). Not before C3 has been tried.

The metamathematics line (owner decision 2026-10-28: main effort; no contact with outside groups). M1: the exact Sherali-Adams degree of the totality of rwPHP(Iter) (Li-Li-Ren, arXiv 2411.15515) and of its parts, with exact rational certificates and pseudo-expectations, towards a composition lemma or an obstruction for Ren's question (can SA prove rwPHP(PLS) totality in polylog degree?) and Davis-Robere OP 4 (Lossy(Iter)). M3: Ref_s(phi) (arXiv 2506.16956 Def. 2.4) in Lean over the library's resolution objects. M2: the refuter problem for NS/PC degree lower bounds of onto-FPHP solved by design evaluation, at (7,8,4) first. Tables are measured; proved only for Lean theorems.

claims.name: K467 (20261104-1627-proof-complexity/K100)
claims.label: proved · independently verified
claims.statement: If $9\mid k$, $n\ge7$, and $\mathrm{Spanning}(3,n+k,n,r)$ for $r=2,3,4$, the degree-four StepSix invariant exists and StdPC has no refutation of $\mathrm{ontoFPHP}(n,k)$ at any degree $d\le4$.

claims.name: K23 (20261024-1110-proof-complexity/K25)
claims.label: proved · independently verified
claims.statement: For $k\ge2$ the cube-connected cycles `Work.CCC.CC k` ($k2^k$ vertices) have degree $\le3$ and the Tseitin formula `HC k` (charge at 0) is unsatisfiable; for $k\ge11$ every resolution refutation (K1's `Refutation`) with $L$ clauses has $(3k2^k)^B\le L(3k2^k-B)^B$, $B=\lfloor 2^k/(8(k+1))\rfloor$.
claims.novelty_note: Known mathematics (Ben-Sasson-Wigderson 2001 width method; CCC expansion Theta(1/log N)). Contribution: core-Lean formalisation of an explicit bounded-degree family, 2^{Omega(|F|/log^4|F|)} in formula size, unconditional.

claims.name: K63 (20261025-0459b-proof-complexity/K7)
claims.label: proved · independently verified
claims.statement: For $L\ge1$, $32L^2\le k-1$, $8L^2k+L\le m$: every tree-like CP refutation `Refutation (CC m k)` (integer coefficients of any size) with $s$ nodes has $2^{L-1}\le s(2k+5)$; at $k-1=32L^2$, $m=8L^2k+L$ this is $2^{\Omega(m^{1/4})}$. Known (Pudlák 1997); formalised.

claims.name: K471 (20261104-1627-proof-complexity/K104)
claims.label: proved · independently verified
claims.statement: For the stored $4\times5$ degree-two canonical top matrix $G$ and explicit sparse $C,H,T$, Lean checks $I_{120}=GC+HT\pmod3$; hence every integer vector with $Tx=0\pmod3$ satisfies $Ix=GCx\pmod3$.

claims.name: K14 (20261024-1110-proof-complexity/K14)
claims.label: proved · independently verified
claims.statement: For every $n\ge3$, every resolution refutation (weakening allowed) of the 3-CNF chain encoding of the ordering principle, `Work.GT3.GT3 n` (not K12's wide encoding), contains a clause with at least $\lfloor (n-1)/2\rfloor$ distinct literals (Bonet–Galesi 2001).
claims.novelty_note: Known result (Bonet–Galesi 2001; proof via the Atserias–Dalmau family criterion). The contribution is the core-Lean formalisation.

claims.name: K21 (20261024-1110-proof-complexity/K22)
claims.label: proved · independently verified
claims.statement: For every $n\ge1$ the Tseitin formula `Work.TseitinK.TK n` of $K_n$ (charge at vertex 0) is unsatisfiable, and for $n\ge41$ every resolution refutation of it (K11's `Refutation`, weakening allowed) has at least $(10/9)^{\lfloor n^2/10\rfloor}$ clauses.
claims.novelty_note: Known (Urquhart 1987; Ben-Sasson-Wigderson 2001 width method). Contribution: core-Lean proof composing a width bound (~n^2/4) with K11; quasi-polynomial in formula size n 2^{n-2}.

claims.name: K22 (20261024-1110-proof-complexity/K23)
claims.label: proved · independently verified
claims.statement: For every $k$ the Tseitin formula `Work.Hypercube.HQ k` of the $k$-dimensional hypercube (charge at vertex 0) is unsatisfiable, and for $k\ge7$ every resolution refutation of it (K1's `Refutation`, weakening allowed) with $L$ clauses has $(8k)^{2^{k-3}}\le L\,(8k-1)^{2^{k-3}}$.
claims.novelty_note: Known mathematics (Tseitin/Urquhart, Ben-Sasson-Wigderson 2001, hypercube isoperimetry). Contribution: core-Lean formalisation; bound 2^{Omega(sqrt|F|/log|F|)} in formula size, unconditional.

claims.name: K54 (20261024-1633-proof-complexity/K26)

claims.statement: $c=\binom\ell2$: (i) $q>0$, $|S|\le\ell$ distinct in $[m]$, $f\ge1$ on $S$-rainbow ⇒ $q^m\le$`tot q (range m) f`$+cq^{m-1}$. claims.name: K7 (20261024-1110-proof-complexity/K7)

claims.statement: For $\mu:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$, $1\le t$: if every line $i\le L$ has $\mu(i)\le 1$ or $\mu(i)\le\mu(a)+\mu(b)$ for some $a,b<i$, and $t<\mu(L)$, then some $j\le L$ has $t<\mu(j)\le 2t$.

claims.name: K12 (20261024-1110-proof-complexity/K12)

claims.novelty_note: Known upper bound (Stålmarck 1996; Bonet–Galesi 2001). New: formal pairing with the width lower bound K14 on one formula, core Lean.
